entries.toelichting: Intense pleading-interjection ('oh, oh!' for prayers, Neh 1, Dan 9, Jonah); the hyphenated English marks the lament-cry.

Sighing or lamenting - in Isaiah 3:26 (her gates shall mourn and lament) and Isaiah 19:8 (the fishers also shall mourn, and all they that cast angle into the river shall lament); root of the lament-noun H592.
Death-by-accident-befallen and calamity-not-overtaking (Ex 21:13; 2Kgs 5:7; Ps 91:10). Hyphenated to distinguish the befall-meet-with-aspect from H7136b qarah-I 'happen-meet'.
Hapax-form; people-to-Jeremiah 'we-ourselves-will-do-as-YHWH-says'; Jer 42:6.
The Aramaic third-person-pronoun 'they' masculine plural - Ezra 5:11, Daniel 2:44, 3:13, 6:25; Aramaic parallel to Hebrew hem.
Second-sense Aramaic innun; four-great-beasts are-four-kings; Dan 7:17.
Collective term for human in his weakness and mortality; poetic parallel for adam; concordantly 'mortal'.
Son of Seth, in whose days men began to call upon the name of YHWH (Gen 4:26; 5:6,7,9,10,11; 1Chr 1:1). 'Mortal-man'. English convention: Enosh.

Niphal: groan/sigh under oppression or grief (Ex 2:23 Israel in Egypt, Prov 29:2, Isa 24:7, Lam 1:4,8,11,21, Eze 9:4 sign on the sighing-ones, 21:6-7,11-12, Joel 1:18 animals-sigh); concordantly 'sigh'.
Feminine noun from anach (sigh, H584); inward-sound-of-suffering (Ex 2:24 'Mighty-One heard their sighing', Job 3:24, 23:2, Ps 6:7 sigh-bed-flooded, 12:6 'sighing of the needy', 31:11, 38:10).
We-servants-of-the-God-of-heaven and we-Aramaic-letter-writers-to-the-king (Ezra 4:16; 5:11; Dan 3:16). Hyphenated to distinguish the we-first-person-plural-aramaic-aspect from Hebrew H587 anachnu.
Personal pronoun 1cp. 'We' standard.
Proper noun, Issachar-city; Josh 19:19; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Anaharath.
Personal pronoun 1cs. Parallel with anokhi (H595).

Seafaring trading-fleet (1Kgs 9:26,27; 10:11,22; 22:49; 2Chr 8:18; 9:21; Isa 33:21; Eze 30:9). Hyphenated to mark the collective-shipping-fleet; distinguished from H591 oniyyah 'ship' (singular-vessel).
Seaworthy vessel; concordantly 'ship'.
Lamentation or sighing - in Isaiah 29:2 (there shall be heaviness and sorrow) and Lamentations 2:5 (mourning and lamentation); feminine abstract from H578 anah (sigh) and pair with H8386 taaniyyah.
Proper noun, Manasseh tribe-head son of Shemida; 1Chr 7:19; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Aniam.

Plumbline-image in Amos-vision over judgment at wall (Amos 7:7 twice; 7:8 twice). Hyphenated to distinguish the plumbline-plummet-aspect from H4949 mishqeleth 'plumbline' and H6957a qav 'measuring-line'.
Personal pronoun 1cs, parallel ani (H589). Semantically equivalent; 'I' in both cases.

Num-people-became-as-complainers-evil-in-ears-of-LORD and Lam-why-does-living-man-complain-of-his-sin (Num 11:1; Lam 3:39). Hyphenated to distinguish the complain-murmur-sigh-aspect from H6049 anan-II 'practise-soothsaying'.
Qal-participle; no-compulsion at Vashti-feast; Esth 1:8.
Aramaic Peal-participle; no-secret-too-difficult-for-Daniel; Dan 4:9.
Qal/Hithpael: nose-snorting feel-anger (YHWH's anger against Solomon); the hyphenated English marks the emotion.
Aramaic parallel to af; face-of-Nebuchadnezzar changed; Dan 3:19.
Lev-stork-heron-after-her-kind-hoopoe-bat and Deut-stork-heron-after-her-kind-hoopoe (Lev 11:19; Deut 14:18). Hyphenated to distinguish the heron-crane-unclean-aspect from other bird-species.
Jer-the-air-filled-groaning and Eze-groaning-Jerusalem-overthrown and Eze-groaning-wounded-glittering (Jer 51:52; Eze 9:4; 24:17; 26:15). Hyphenated to distinguish the groan-cry-out-loudly-aspect.
Sighing-sound of prisoners and wounded (Ps 12:6; 79:11; 102:21; Mal 2:13). Hyphenated to distinguish the groan-moan-lament-aspect from H7581 she'agah 'roar' and H4116 mahar 'lament-cry'.
Unclean creeping-creature wall-gecko-species; Lev 11:30; concordantly transliterated.
Cling-to-an-illness to fatally-incurable (2Sam 12:15; Job 34:6; Ps 69:21; Jer 15:18; 17:9,16; 30:12,15; Mic 1:9). Hyphenated to distinguish the chronic-fatal-character from H2470 chalah 'be-sick'.
Aramaic noun: man, human; parallel to Hebrew enosh; concordantly hyphenated with language-marker.
Aramaic personal pronoun 2ms; parallel to Hebrew attah; concordantly 'you-aramaic'.
Aramaic personal pronoun 2p plural (Dan 2:8); cognate Hebrew attem.
Proper noun; king of Judah; concordantly transliterated.
Small oil-vessel of Elisha-widow; 2Kgs 4:2.
Fatal-disastrous incident affecting body (Gen 42:4,38; 44:29; Ex 21:22,23). Hyphenated to distinguish the calamity-mishap-aspect from H7451 ra 'evil-misery'.
Judg-the-cords-which-were-on-his-arms-became-as-flax-burned-with-fire-and-his-bands-melted-from-his-hands and Eccl-better-poor-young-man-than-old-king-who-no-longer-knows-how-to-receive-admonition.
Royal-punishment-fine-up-to-imprisonment and Daniel-bound-not-permitted and bonds-imprisonment-edict (Ezra 7:26; Dan 4:12,20). Hyphenated.

Ex-feast-of-ingathering-at-the-going-out-of-the-year and Ex-feast-of-ingathering-turn-of-the-year (Ex 23:16; 34:22). Hyphenated to distinguish the in-gathering-harvest-aspect from H625 osef 'harvest'.
From √asar (bind); held in chains (Egyptian prisoners, Joseph); concordantly 'prisoner'.

Collective-prisoners as group of afflicted (Isa 10:4; 24:22; Ps 79:11; 102:21). Hyphenated to distinguish the prisoner-collective-aspect from homonym H615 asir-I 'prisoner-singular' (already assigned).
In chains-bound war-prisoner (Gen 39:20,22; Isa 10:4; 14:17; 24:22; 42:7; Ps 68:7; 69:34; 79:11; 102:21; 107:10; 146:7; Lam 3:34; Zech 9:11). Hyphenated to distinguish the fettered-captive-aspect.

Deut-the-LORD-shall-command-the-blessing-on-you-in-your-barns-and-in-all-that-you-set-your-hand-to and Prov-so-shall-your-barns-be-filled-with-plenty-and-your-presses-burst-out-with-new-wine (Deut 28:8; Prov 3:10).
Proper noun, father of Nethinim-clan returnees; Ezra 2:50; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Asnah.
Persian-king Ezra 4:10 who deported peoples; identification Asherbanipal of Assyria.
Asenath-daughter-of-Potipherah-priest-of-On and wife-of-Joseph (Gen 41:45,50; 46:20). English convention: Asenath. Egyptian 'belonging-to-Neith' or 'favourite-of-Neith' (Neith = Egyptian-goddess).
Root 'sp. 'Gather' standard; also 'take-up' (to die = gathered-to-fathers).
Proper noun ('he-gathered'); Levite-singer under David; concordantly transliterated.
Gatekeepers-at-the-houses-of-the-storehouse and temple-stores-gathering-places (1Chr 26:15,17; Neh 12:25). Hyphenated to distinguish the storehouse-warehouse-gathering-place-aspect from H214 otsar.
Isa-as-in-harvest-he-gathers-sheaves and Mic-harvest-time-seeking-grapes and Isa-harvest-ingathering-of-fathers (Isa 32:10; 33:4; Mic 7:1). Hyphenated.
Prisoners-gathered in pit-confined; Isa 24:22.
Hapax Eccl 12:11 masters-of-collections; from H622 asaph gather.
Together-gathered-mixed-multitude joining-the-exodus; Num 11:4.
Persian loanword 'precisely/diligently' in Daniel-Ezra (Ezra 5:8; 6:8,12,13; 7:17,21,26). Hyphenated to preserve the Persian-administrative diligence; concordantly via '-aramaic'.
Proper noun, third son of Haman; Esth 9:7; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Aspatha.
Qal: bind fast, put in fetters; concordantly 'bind' across all contexts (captive, obligation, harnessing horse).
From √asar (bind, H631); self-imposed vow-binding-obligation (Num 30:2-14 complete legislation about female vows that can be annulled by father or husband); concordantly 'binding-vow'.
Aramaic 'forbidding-binding-decree' in Daniel's lions'-den-narrative (Dan 6:8,9,10,13,14,16). Hyphenated; concordantly via '-aramaic'; family with Hebrew issar.
Proper noun, son of Sennacherib successor in Assyria; Isa 37:38; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Esar-haddon.
Proper noun (possibly Persian sterre = star); queen in Esther; concordantly transliterated.
Aramaic-building-wood for temple-construction (Ezra 5:8; 6:4,11; Dan 5:4,23). Hyphenated to mark the Aramaic-parallel; distinguished from Hebrew H6086 ets 'tree-wood'.
Additive-escalative particle. Homograph with af (nose/anger, H639). Functionally 'yea-even' or 'moreover'; 'if even'.
Aramaic-additive 'also-with-existing' (Ezra 5:10,14; 6:5; Dan 6:22). Hyphenated to distinguish the also-likewise-aspect from H1571 gam 'also' (already assigned); Aramaic cognate.
Root 'np. Anatomically 'nose', idiomatically 'anger' (swollen nostrils). 'Nose' preserves the anatomical kernel that carries through both fields; 'anger' loses the anatomical basis.

Ex-you-shall-gird-him-with-the-cunningly-woven-ephod and Lev-Moses-girded-him-with-the-cunningly-woven-ephod (Ex 29:5; Lev 8:7). Hyphenated to distinguish the ephod-gird-don-aspect from H247 azar 'gird'.
Proper noun, father of Hanniel Manasseh-leader; Num 34:23; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ephod.
Ex-girdle-ephod-which-is-on-it-of-like-work and Isa-you-shall-defile-covering-of-silver-graven-images (Ex 28:8; 29:5; Isa 30:22). Hyphenated.
King-shall-pitch-his-palace-tents between-seas; Dan 11:45.
Qal: prepare bread on hot stone or in oven; concordantly 'bake'.
Emphatic particle in questions/reasonings: 'where then', 'what then'; the hyphenated English marks the question-emphasis.
Cultic priestly garment with breastplate; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun, ancestor of Saul; 1Sam 9:1; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Aphiah.
Spelt and rye not yet grown out; Ex 9:32.
1Chr-and-the-sons-of-Nadab-Seled-and-Appaim and 1Chr-and-the-sons-of-Appaim-Ishi (1Chr 2:30,31). Hyphenated.
Deep riverbed, channel through which water flows; the hyphenated English marks the object.
Day-of-the-LORD-not-light-but dark-without-shine; Amos 5:20.
Dense, massive darkness; heavier than choshek (Job 3:6; 10:22; 23:17; 28:3; 30:26; Ps 11:2; 91:6; Isa 29:18; 58:10). Hyphenated to distinguish intensity-degree from H2822 choshek 'darkness'.
Deep-dark distinguished from choshek (darkness, H2822) by intensity-of-density (Ex 10:22 'three-days-darkness in Egypt felt', Deut 28:29 'groping at noon as blind in darkness').
1Chr-and-Zabad-begat-Ephlal-and-Ephlal-begat-Obed (1Chr 2:37,37). Hyphenated.
Word-at-right-moment-as-golden-apples; Prov 25:11.
Completely-dry-up or cease-to-exist (Gen 47:15,16; Isa 16:4; 29:20; Ps 77:9). Hyphenated to distinguish the exhausted-aspect from H3615 kalah 'complete-end'; family with H657a efes.
Substantive: utmost end, non-existent, nothingness; concordantly 'nothing'.
Second-sense efes; water-reaching-to-ankles; Eze 47:3.
Proper noun ('boundary-of-bloods') battle-place David-Goliath; 1Sam 17:1; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ephes-dammim.
Idol-works are nothing-and-empty; Isa 41:24.
Wicked-viper-venom-suck and Isa-viper-in-desert and Isa-snake-eggs-hatch (Job 20:16; Isa 30:6; 59:5). Hyphenated to distinguish the viper-poisonous-snake-aspect from H5175 nachash.

Water-streams or enemies threateningly surrounding (2Sam 22:5; Ps 18:5; 40:13; 116:3; Jonah 2:6). Hyphenated to distinguish the encompass-enclose-aspect from H5437 savav 'go-around' and H3803 kathar 'crown'.
Strong-inward-restraining of emotion (Gen 43:31; 45:1; Esth 5:10; Isa 42:14; 63:15; 64:11). Hyphenated to preserve the reflexive-restraint.
Several-places: Asherite-city (Josh 19:30 = Judg 1:31), Philistine-army-camp against-Israel (1Sam 4:1, 29:1), Aram-battle-place (1Kgs 20:26,30; 2Kgs 13:17). English convention: Aphek.
Proper noun, Judah-hill-country-city; Josh 15:53; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Aphekah.
Burnt-residue; sign of mourning and transience; concordantly 'ashes'.
1K-and-the-prophet-went-and-stood-before-the-king-on-the-way-and-disguised-himself-with-ashes-on-his-eyes and 1K-and-he-hastened-and-took-the-ashes-from-his-eyes (1K 20:38,41). Hyphenated.
Chicks of bird-of-prey or mother-dove (Deut 22:6; Job 39:30; Ps 84:4). Hyphenated to preserve the young-chicks-aspect.
Solomon's-palanquin from Lebanon-wood; Song 3:9.
Proper noun. English convention Ephraim.
Aramaic gentilic exiles-people (Ezra 4:9); possibly Persian-Apharis.
One of the Persian people-groups colonised by Asnappar (Ashurbanipal) in Samaria, opposing the temple-rebuilding - Ezra 5:6, 6:6; presumably Persian officials or state-administrators.
Aramaic-Persian official-group (Ezra 4:9); alongside H671a Apharsachite variant of the same group.

Older-name for Bethlehem-area (Gen 35:16,19 Rachel-burial-place, 48:7 Jacob's-recollection); David's ethnic-origin (1Sam 17:12 'Ephrathite of Bethlehem', Ruth 1:2, 4:11). English convention: Ephrath / Ephratah.
Tribal-designation for Ephraimite or Bethlehemite (Judg 12:5; 1Sam 1:1; 17:12; 1Kgs 11:26; Ruth 1:2). Gentilic; family with H672 Ephrath.
Aramaic-Persian-loan royal-treasury-revenue (Ezra 4:13); word-stem Persian.
Gen-sons-Gad-Haggi-Shuni-Ezbon-Eri and Num-sons-Gad-Ozni (Gen 46:16; Num 26:16). Hyphenated; Gad-fourth-son-later-variant-Ozni-Num.
Finger of human or metaphor for God's working; concordantly 'finger'.
Aramaic parallel to etsba; man's-hand-fingers writing; Dan 5:5.
Ex-against-the-nobles-of-Israel-He-stretched-out-not-His-hand and Isa-from-the-ends-of-the-earth-you-nobles (Ex 24:11; Isa 41:9). Hyphenated.
Jer-in-armpits-under-arm-joints-rags and Eze-near-joints-of-hands and Eze-joints-of-arms (Jer 38:12; Eze 13:18; 41:8). Hyphenated to distinguish the joint-elbow-limb-aspect from H6504 parad.
Isaac's-blessing-for-Esau-not-reserved and Moses-spirit-imparted on seventy-elders (Gen 27:36; Num 11:17,25; Eze 42:6). Hyphenated to distinguish the set-apart-reserve-impart-aspect from H914 badal.
Preposition: alongside, near; concordantly 'beside' (spatial proximity).
Benjamite descendant of Jonathan (1Chr 8:37,38; 9:43,44). English convention: Azel.
Second-sense atsal; people-shall-flee-along-mountain-cleft; Zech 14:5.

2K-the-king-sent-Shaphan-the-son-of-Azaliah-the-son-of-Meshullam-the-scribe-to-the-house-of-the-LORD and 2Chr-the-king-sent-Shaphan-the-son-of-Azaliah-and-Maaseiah-the-governor-of-the-city (2K 22:3; 2Chr 34:8).
1Chr-Ozem-the-sixth-and-David-the-seventh and 1Chr-Ozem-was-the-fourth-Ither-the-fifth (1Chr 2:15; 2:25). Hyphenated.
Num-brought-offering-armlet-ring-signet-ring-earring-necklace-atonement-souls and 2S-I-took-crown-on-head-and-armlet-on-arm (Num 31:50; 2S 1:10). Hyphenated.
Pile-up valuables in storage-chambers (2Kgs 20:17; Isa 39:6; Amos 3:10; Neh 13:12,13). Hyphenated to preserve the treasure-storing-aspect; family with H214 otsar 'treasury'.
Horite tribe-head among Seir's sons (Gen 36:21,27,30; 1Chr 1:38,42). English convention: Ezer.
Zion's-gates of ruby-stones; Isa 54:12.
Clean food-species; Deut 14:5.
Proper noun, Asher-tribe-head son of Jether; 1Chr 7:38; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ara.
Battle-heroes-cry-bitterly outside-city; Isa 33:7.
Areli-son-of-Gad and clan-genealogy (Gen 46:16; Num 26:17 twice). English convention: Areli. 'Lion-of-God' or 'hero-of-God'.
Qal: lie in ambush, wait to overtake; concordantly 'lie-in-wait'.
Proper noun, Judah-hill-country-city; Josh 15:52; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Arab.
The robbery-ambush of wild beasts - Job 37:8 (the wild beasts go into the den and remain in their dwellings) and 38:40 (when they lie in ambush to take prey); from H693 arav (lie-in-wait).
People's-tongue-arrow is craft-deceit; Jer 9:8.
From √rabah (multiply); swarm-locust as plague; concordantly 'locust' (distinguished from gazam, chasil).
Moab struggles-with-arms in dung-pit; Isa 25:11.
Window-shutter at top; at flood and at blessing/judgment-opening of heaven (Gen 7:11; 8:2; Mal 3:10; Eccl 12:3; Hos 13:3; Isa 24:18; 60:8). Hyphenated so that the cosmic function is visible.
Solomon-district 1Kgs 4:10 with Socoh and land of Hepher; place-name plural-form.
Patronym-clan David's-warrior Paarai; 2Sam 23:35; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Arbite.
Cardinal numeral. 'Four' standard.
Aramaic four in the Aramaic portions (Ezra 6:17; Dan 3:25; 7:2,3,6,17). Cognate of Hebrew H702. Concordantly via '-aramaic'.
Multiplicative of arba (H702). 'Forty' standard.
David's-own-judgment fourfold restoration; 2Sam 12:6.
Qal: cross threads on loom (priestly-clothing, blankets); concordantly 'weave'.
Judg-and-he-pulled-them-out-with-the-weaver's-beam-and-the-web and Job-my-days-have-been-swifter-than-a-weaver's-shuttle-and-have-vanished-without-hope (Judg 16:14; Job 7:6). Hyphenated.
Bashan-region with fortified cities (Deut 3:4,13,14; 2Kgs 15:25). English convention: Argob. 'Earth-clod-region'.
Solomon-temple-cloth requested from Hiram; 2Chr 2:7.
Dan-aramaic-clothed-with-purple and Dan-aramaic-clothed-with-purple-Daniel and Dan-aramaic-promise-of-purple-garment (Dan 5:7,16,29). Hyphenated.

Ark-cows-cart-argaz-beside-ark and Philistines-trespass-offering-in-chest (1Sam 6:8,11,15). Hyphenated to distinguish the chest-travel-chest-baggage-chest-aspect from H727 aron 'ark-chest' (already assigned).
Expensive red-purple dye from sea-snail; colour of nobility and sanctuary; concordantly 'purple'.
Gen-sons-Benjamin-Bela-Becher-Ashbel-Gera-Naaman-Ehi-Rosh-Muppim-Huppim-Ard and Num-sons-Benjamin-Ard (Gen 46:21; Num 26:40). Hyphenated.
Proper noun, son of Caleb; 1Chr 2:18; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ardon.
Patronym-clan son of Benjamin; Num 26:40; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ardite.
Pluck or pick fruits-vine-leaves - in Psalm 80:13 (all who pass by the way pluck him) and Song of Songs 5:1 (I gather my myrrh with my spice); concrete action of breaking off.
Aramaic-deictic interjection in visions (Dan 7:2,5,6,7,8,13). Hyphenated to mark the Aramaic-parallel; distinguished from Hebrew H7200 ra'ah 'see'.

Proper noun Arvad (Phoenician island-city, modern Ruad) - in Ezekiel 27:8 (the inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers) and Ezekiel 27:11 (the men of Arvad with your army were on your walls round about).
Proper noun, son of Gad; Num 26:17; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Arod.
Gen-Canaan-begat-Sidon-Heth-Jebusite-Amorite-Girgashite-Hivite-Arkite-Sinite-Arvadite and 1Chr-Arvadite (Gen 10:18; 1Chr 1:16). Hyphenated.
Gen-and-the-sons-of-Gad-Ziphion-and-Haggi-Arodi-and-Areli and Num-of-Arod-the-family-of-the-Arodites (Gen 46:16; Num 26:17). Hyphenated.
1K-Solomon-had-forty-thousand-horse-stalls-for-his-chariots and 2Chr-Solomon-had-four-thousand-horse-stalls-and-chariots (1K 4:26 par; 2Chr 9:25; cf 32:28). Hyphenated.
Healing-of wound or people-destruction (2Chr 24:13; Neh 4:1; Jer 8:22; 30:17; 33:6; Isa 58:8). Hyphenated to distinguish the healing-restoration-aspect from H4832 marpe 'healing' and H7499 refuah.
Proper noun, place where Abimelech stayed; Judg 9:41; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Arumah.
Text-uncertain variant Aramim/Adomim Elath-context; 2Kgs 16:6.
Unique lexeme. Wooden chest (covenant-ark, coffin, money-chest). 'Ark' covers all contexts; 'chest' is competing but 'ark' is the standard convention for this specific lexeme.
Jebusite-owner of-threshing-floor-on-Moriah where David-altar-built after-plague-halt (2Sam 24:16,18,20-24 core-account). English convention: Araunah.
Qal-passive-participle; firmly-bound cedar-beams; Eze 27:24.
Cedar-tree (cedrus libani); concordantly 'cedar'; same tree-species across all contexts.
Nineveh's-cedar-panelling-exposed; Zeph 2:14.
Old-man-wayfarer-Gibeah and Job-wayfarer-with-the-wicked and traveller-disciplining (Judg 19:17; Job 34:8; Ps 139:3). Hyphenated to distinguish the travel-journey-wayfarer-aspect from H1980 halakh.
Asherite family-head and post-exile-family-ancestor (1Chr 7:39; Ezra 2:5; Neh 6:18; 7:10). English convention: Arah. 'Wayfarer-traveller'.
Beaten path, often poetic; distinguished from derech (way) and mesillah (highway); concordantly 'path'.
Aramaic word for path or conduct - in Daniel 4:37 (all His ways are right) and Daniel 5:23 (the God in whose hand your breath is and to whom all your paths belong); parallel of Hebrew orach.
Gen-caravan-Ishmaelites-came-from-Gilead-camels-laden and Isa-behold-caravan-Dedanites (Gen 37:25; Isa 21:13). Hyphenated to distinguish the caravan-travellers-aspect from H734 orach 'path'.
Fixed-allotted food-ration for prisoner or guest (2Kgs 25:30; Jer 40:5; 52:34; Prov 15:17). Hyphenated to preserve the fixed-food-portion.
Gad-warriors with lion-faces; 1Chr 12:8.
Variant-spelling of aryeh; concordantly 'lion-II' (same species, parallel in poetic texts).
Adult lion as predator and image of strength; concordantly 'lion' (distinguished from kefir young-lion).
2S-Benaiah-struck-two-strong-lions-of-Moab and 1Chr-Benaiah-the-son-of-Jehoiada-struck-two-strong-lions-of-Moab (2S 23:20; 1Chr 11:22). Hyphenated.
Mighty-man of David, prophetic-name of Jerusalem (2Sam 23:20; 1Chr 11:22; Ezra 8:16; Isa 29:1,2,7). 'Lion-of-God'. English convention: Ariel.

Altar-hearth or fire-hearth of God (literally 'lion-of-God') - in Ezekiel 43:15 (the altar-hearth shall be four cubits) and Ezekiel 43:16 (the altar-hearth shall be twelve cubits in length); burnt-offering.
Proper noun, ninth son of Haman; Esth 9:9; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Aridai.
Proper noun, sixth son of Haman; Esth 9:8; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Aridatha.
Aramaic cognate of ari (lion, H738b); exclusive in Dan 6:8,13,17,20-21,25,28, 7:4 'first-beast like-lion, eagle's-wings had-it' - symbolic-empire-image.
Proper noun, fellow-killer with Pekah against Pekahiah; 2Kgs 15:25; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Arieh.
Gen-Arioch-king-Ellasar-in-coalition-with-Amraphel and Gen-same-kings-repetition and Dan-Arioch-head-of-king's-bodyguard (Gen 14:1,9; Dan 2:14,15,24,25). Hyphenated.
Aramaic form Babylonian-king's-guard-captain (Dan 2:14-25); alongside H746a Arioch-Elam-king Gen 14.
Proper noun, eighth son of Haman; Esth 9:9; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Arisai.
Qal/Hiphil: extend in time or space, prolong; the hyphenated English marks state.
Aramaic fitting-proper (Ezra 4:14 not-fitting-king-dishonour).
From √arach (be-long); long-of-nose (delaying anger), attribute of YHWH 'long-suffering and merciful'; the hyphenated English marks the patient-restrained-anger.
Proper noun, city in Shinar; Gen 10:10; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Erech.

Rabshakeh-speak-in-Aramaic-not-in-Judaic and Daniel-Aramaic-answer and Ezra-letter-in-Aramaic (2Kgs 18:26; Dan 2:4; Ezra 4:7). Hyphenated.
Mesopotamian Syria between-two-rivers (Gen 24:10; Deut 23:5; Judg 3:8; Ps 60:2). Compound 'Aram-of-the-two-rivers'; family with H758 Aram.

Gen-sons-Dishan-Uz-Aran and 1Chr-sons-Dishan-Uz-Aran (Gen 36:28; 1Chr 1:42). Hyphenated.

Lev-hare-because-it-chews-cud-but-does-not-divide-hoof-unclean and Deut-camel-hare-rabbit-not-eat-unclean (Lev 11:6; Deut 14:7). Hyphenated.

Proper noun, descendant of David post-exile; 1Chr 3:21; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Arnan.
Jebusite-thresher whose threshing-floor David bought as temple-site (1Chr 21:15-28, 2Chr 3:1); parallel to Araunah in 2Sam 24; concordantly transliterated.

Aramaic parallel to erets; idols-without-earth-making; Jer 10:11.
Qal: curse (call down evil); distinguished from qalal (consider light/curse); concordantly 'curse'.

Piel: betroth as legally-binding pre-marriage-promise (Ex 22:16, Deut 20:7, 22:23-28, 28:30, 2Sam 3:14 David-Michal). Concordantly 'betroth'.
Lips-petition of king not-withheld; Ps 21:2.
Persian sovereign Artaxerxes in Ezra and Nehemiah (Ezra 4:7,8,11,23; 7:1,7,11,12,21; 8:1; Neh 2:1; 5:14; 13:6). English convention: Artaxerxes.
Persian-king Artaxerxes in alternative-spelling. English convention: Artaxerxes-variant. Distinguished from H783a.
Unique lexeme. 'Fire' standard.

The foundations of the rebuilt temple - Ezra 4:12, 5:16, 6:3; Aramaic, possibly Persian loanword, related to walls-foundation H846 ushrana.
Ashbel-son-of-Benjamin and clan-genealogy (Gen 46:21; Num 26:38; 1Chr 8:1). English convention: Ashbel. 'Man-of-Baal' or 'fire-of-Baal'.
Patronym-clan son of Benjamin; Num 26:38; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ashbelite.
Proper noun, son of Dishan; Gen 36:26; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Eshban.

1Chr-and-Saul-begat-Jonathan-and-Malchishua-and-Abinadab-and-Eshbaal and 1Chr-id (1Chr 8:33; 9:39 par). Hyphenated.
Mountain-slope-water-stream-incline; Num 21:15.
Mountain-slopes on the east side of the Dead Sea (Deut 3:17; 4:49; Josh 10:40; 12:3,8; 13:20). 'Slopes'. English convention: Ashdoth.
Proper noun; city of the Philistine pentapolis, centre of the Dagon-cult; concordantly transliterated.
Inhabitant of the Philistine city Ashdod (Josh 13:3; 1Sam 5:6,7; Neh 4:1; 13:23,24). Gentilic; family with H795 Ashdod.
Half-blood-children spoke Ashdodite tongue; Neh 13:24.
Fiery-law from the right hand of YHWH; Deut 33:2.
Lead-consumed-in-fire vainly-refining; Jer 6:29.
From √esh (fire); offering consumed by fire; the hyphenated English preserves the burnt-cultic dimension.
Root 'nsh; female counterpart ish (H376). Also 'wife'; context decides.
Foundation or supporting stone-work - in Isaiah 16:7 (you shall mourn for the foundations of Kir-Hareseth) and parallel-text; architecture-base of Moabite city-bulwark in oracle.

Proper noun people, descendant of Dedan; Gen 25:3; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Asshurim.
Hapax 2Sam 2:9 preposition-variant; orthographic form alongside the standard H413 el.
1Chr-after-the-death-of-Hezron-in-Caleb-Ephrathah-Abijah-the-wife-of-Hezron-bore-him-Ashhur-the-father-of-Tekoa and 1Chr-Ashhur-the-father-of-Tekoa-had-two-wives-Helah-and-Naarah (1Chr 2:24; 4:5).
Proper noun, Hamath-deity; 2Kgs 17:30; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ashima.
Hapax Isa 16:7 Moab-lament-cry; lament-cry woe-to-me.
Raisin-cake as love-comfort or feast-gift (2Sam 6:19; 1Chr 16:3; Hos 3:1; Song 2:5). Hyphenated to distinguish the raisin-cake-aspect from H6778 tsimmuq 'raisin-cake' and H5692 ugah.
Testicle; body-part-defect; Lev 21:20.
Cluster of grapes; explicit in the spies-episode and the parables of Isaiah (Gen 40:10; Num 13:23,24; Deut 32:32; Song 1:14; 7:7,8,9; Isa 65:8; Mic 7:1). Hyphenated.
Ally of Abraham and the name-giving valley near Hebron (Gen 14:13,24; Num 13:23,24; 32:9; Deut 1:24). English convention: Eshcol. Family with H811 eshkol 'cluster-of-grapes'.
Ashkenaz-people-son of Gomer and war-call against Babel (Gen 10:3; 1Chr 1:6; Jer 51:27). English convention: Ashkenaz. 'Scytho-Cimmerian-people'.
The gift-tribute that peoples bring to Zion or the trading-partner - Psalm 72:10 (the kings of Tarshish and the isles shall offer presents) and Ezekiel 27:15 (they brought you in payment).
Abraham's-tamarisk in Beersheba and Saul-resting-place (Gen 21:33; 1Sam 22:6; 31:13). Distinguished from H427 alah 'oak' and H424 elah 'terebinth' (already assigned) and H436 elon.
Qal: take guilt upon oneself; Niphal: be found guilty; the hyphenated English marks state.

From √asham (be-guilty); state of guilt and the awareness of it; the hyphenated English marks the inward burden.
People-grope-in-fatness-darkness as-the-dead; Isa 59:10.
